submission.justification: Crystal-K2 has the best resolution (2.9% FWHM at 662 keV), but the Q1 2026 assay measured its intrinsic background at 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day. That is 4 times the hard 0.5 counts/kg/day budget, so K2 is ruled out. Of the two crystals that pass, K3 has much better resolution (4.5% vs 8.5% for K1) and a background of 0.30 ± 0.05, which is within budget. The thickness is 5 cm because that is the nominal thickness used in the 2025 simulation, where resolution changed little between 3 and 8 cm. No simulation tool was available, so I did not run a thickness optimisation. The background limit is given per kg, so thickness does not affect whether K3 passes.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K3 has 4.5% FWHM, the best of the crystals that meet the background budget (K1: 8.5%). K2 is better at 2.9% but fails the background budget. Source: simulation_summary_2025.md.

requirements.requirement: Crystal must be one of the three candidates
Intrinsic background (100-3000 keV) at or below 0.5 counts/kg/day (hard)
requirements.evidence: K3 measured 0.30 ± 0.05 counts/kg/day in the 30-day underground HPGe assay (assay_campaign_2026Q1.md). K2 measured 2.0 ± 0.2 and fails.
5 cm is within the range. It is the simulated nominal thickness, and resolution depended only weakly on thickness from 3 to 8 cm.
